Changelog

Source: NEWS.md

RiskScorescvd 0.4.0

This release changes SCORE2() / SCORE2_CKD() results for some patients (see the breaking changes below). Results for everyone else are identical to 0.3.1, which was verified against the 0.3.1 release on a grid of more than 35,000 input combinations and on calc_scores().

Bug fix: SCORE2 classification for ages between 69 and 70

  • For non-integer ages between 69 and 70 (e.g. 69.5), classify = TRUE in SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD() returned a function instead of a risk group, because the age bands were defined as <= 69 and >= 70. The 50-69 band now covers ages up to 70, matching the SCORE2 / SCORE2-OP age split. Risk categories follow the 2021 ESC prevention guidelines (doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehab484). Whole-number ages are unaffected.

Other

  • Corrected the SCORE2-Diabetes DOI in DESCRIPTION (ehad260).
  • Documentation: “creatine” corrected to “creatinine” (GRACE creat, CKD ACR), typo fixes, risk-category source cited, README link updated.

Missing inputs in SCORE2 and SCORE2_CKD give NA with a warning (#21)

  • If any required input is NA, SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD() return NA with a warning naming the missing input(s). A missing Age, Gender or Risk.region previously stopped with “missing value where TRUE/FALSE needed”, which in calc_scores() stopped the whole data frame. Other missing inputs already gave NA, but silently. ACR and trace remain optional.

New: SCORE2 and SCORE2_CKD accept vectors (#18)

  • SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD() now accept vector inputs (each of length 1 or n) and return a vector, without needing dplyr::rowwise(). Results are identical to scoring row by row. Mismatched lengths give an informative error.

Breaking change: SCORE2 no longer scores people under 40 (#17)

  • SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD() now return NA with a warning for patients aged under 40. SCORE2 was developed and validated for ages 40-69 (doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehab309). The data-frame wrappers and calc_scores() inherit this.

Breaking change: SCORE2 no longer scores people with diabetes under 70 (#15)

  • SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD() now return NA with a warning for patients aged under 70 with diabetes = 1. SCORE2 is not intended for, or validated in, people with diabetes. The diabetes coefficients came from the derivation model used for recalibration, not from the published risk algorithm (SCORE2 working group 2021, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehab309; Hageman et al. 2022, doi:10.1093/eurheartj/ehab761, Table 1 footnote). Use SCORE2_Diabetes() for these patients.
  • SCORE2_scores(), SCORE2_CKD_scores() and calc_scores() inherit this: their SCORE2 columns are now NA for those rows.
  • No change for people without diabetes, or for anyone aged 70 or over (SCORE2-OP includes diabetes as a predictor).
  • Thanks to @meehownow for the report.
  • SCORE2 and SCORE2-CKD examples now use patients without diabetes.
  • diabetes can now be omitted in SCORE2() and SCORE2_CKD(): it is then assumed to be 0 (no diabetes), with a warning so the assumption is never silent. Calls that pass diabetes, including the data-frame wrappers and calc_scores(), are unaffected.

RiskScorescvd 0.3.1

CRAN release: 2025-08-27

CRAN resubmission fix

  • Updated R version requirement from >= 3.1.0 to >= 4.1.0 to match native pipe syntax usage
  • No functional changes to package code

RiskScorescvd 0.3.0

Major testing and documentation improvements

  • Comprehensive test suite added with 328 tests achieving 93.98% coverage
  • New vignette with practical examples and distribution plots added
  • All functions now have extensive unit tests covering edge cases and error handling
  • Package dependencies properly declared in DESCRIPTION
  • Enhanced package reliability and documentation quality
